Shows how the backup to your USB drive is going
No USB drive has been authorized
The last backup was interrupted by the system. Open the app and tap “Back up to USB drive” to pick up where it left off — nothing already copied will be sent again.
The task failed and reported no reason
%1$s is larger than 4 GB — FAT32 drives cannot hold a file that big (format the drive as exFAT and the limit goes away). Original error: %2$s
Do not back up this folder
Divider between the two cards — drag or tap it to switch layout. Currently %1$s
%1$d failed — this backup ran before failure logging existed, so there are no details
Nothing new was copied this time

“%1$s” can only be read from, not written to. Either the drive’s write-protect switch is on, or it is formatted as NTFS (which Android usually mounts read-only) — reformat it as exFAT and it will work.
“%1$s” is not plugged in. The permission is still there — plug it back in and you can carry on.
The USB drive is full. Free up some space and tap retry — nothing already copied will be sent again. Original error: %1$s
Cannot write to this drive. Either its write-protect switch is on, or it is formatted as NTFS (which Android usually mounts read-only) — reformat it as exFAT and it will work. Original error: %1$s
The system will not let the app write to this drive. Unplug it, plug it back in and pick the folder again. Original error: %1$s
Something went wrong reading or writing the drive — usually a loose connection or a bad sector. Try another port or another cable. Original error: %1$s
The USB drive was disconnected part-way through. Plug it back in and tap retry — nothing already copied will be sent again. Original error: %1$s
That photo is no longer on the phone (it may have just been deleted). Original error: %1$s
The system revoked access to this drive. Pick the USB folder again to carry on. Original error: %1$s
Could not create “%1$s” on the USB drive. Usually this means the drive is full, write-protected, or was unplugged — check and tap retry.
Could not open the backup folder on the USB drive. The drive may have been unplugged, or the permission may have lapsed. Plug it back in, and pick the folder again if needed.
The backup marker file on this drive could not be read (%1$s). The drive may have been written by other software, or the file may be damaged.
There are already hundreds of copies of “%1$s” on the drive, so numbering stopped here.
